item.title: UHSAA associate director Jeff Cluff, 49, dies from complications from stroke
item.description: Jeff Cluff, UHSAA associate director Jeff Cluff, who spent the past 12 years as a director with the UHSAA and was a champion of the mission of high school athletics, passed away at t. George Regional Hospital late Wednesday evening surrounded by family after complications from a stroke. He was 49. Cluff suffered a stroke last year Thursday, and after the family updated his condition on social media Saturday, they received an outpouring of love and support from the thousands and thousands of people in the athletics community who Cluff impacted. UHSAA associate director Jeff Cluff presents the state championship trophy to Corner Canyon after winning the 6A girls volleyball state championship against Skyridge at the UCCU Center at Utah Valley University in Orem on Thursday, Oct. 30, 2025. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News Cluff joined the UHSAA in 2014 as the supervisor of officials. During his time with the UHSAA, he’s also served as the director of baseball, along with overseeing compliance and eligibility, media services, arbiter sports, website administration, ticketing operations and numerous other roles. Prior to that he worked 13 years in the Dixie State University (now utah Tech) athletics department. Here’s the official family statement through social media on Thursday morning. View this post on Instagram “It is with profound sadness that we announce the death of our beloved husband, father, brother, son and friend, Jeff cluff, 49, following complications from a stroke. Jeff died late Wednesday evening surrounded by loved ones. Born in Tooele, Utah, jeff built a life centered on faith, family, friendship and service to others. He had a remarkable ability to make everyone he encountered fell like the most important person in the room. He was genuine, fiercely loyal, quick-witted and unapologetically himself. He told you what you needed to hear, stood by you when it mattered most and was always looking for ways to help others. These were values he and Monica worked to instill in their children, because raising a good family was his life’s mission. Whether on a the baseball field, among friends or at home with his family, Jeff lived with integrity, kindness and a deep sense of fairness. Those who knew him as an umpire knew the same man we knew at home: honest, consistent, firm in his convictions and kind at heart. Jeff’s generosity extended far beyond those closest to him, and in keeping with his lifelong commitment to helping others, Jeff’s final act of generosity was to give the gift of life through organ donation, hopefully blessing the lives of others as he did ours. While our hearts are broken, we find comfort in our faith, the memories we share adn the extraordinary outpouring of love from the community. Hearing the countless stories of how Jeff touched the lives of others has been a tremendous source of strength for our family. The greatest tribute anyone could offer Jeff is to carry forward the qualities that defined him: show up for others

item.title: “RIZE Up Day” aims to empower Western PA middle schoolers
item.description: WPXI Approximately 200 middle school students from the Aliquippa and Shaler Area school districts gathered at the RIZE Sports Complex in Leetsdale on Tuesday for “RIZE Up Day.” The four-hour program engaged sixth-, seventh- and eighth-grade students in sports training, health workshops and career exploration. Organized by the Boys & Girls Clubs of Western Pennsylvania and hosted by RIZE Sports, the event took place at 1201 Brickworks Dr. Program organizers structured the day to help young people build confidence, maintain active lifestyles and learn about career opportunities in the sports and wellness industries. Chuck Cooper III addressed the students as the keynote speaker following opening remarks. Cooper is the president and chief executive officer of the Chuck Cooper Foundation. He is the son of Charles “Chuck” Cooper, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame member who became the first African American drafted into the NBA. Participants took part in physical training spread across three activity rotations. Community coaches from the Cleveland Cavaliers directed basketball skills sessions, while players from the University of Pittsburgh women’s lacrosse team led agility and conditioning drills. Beyond athletics, the morning incorporated wellness and emergency response education. Representatives from the Children’s Institute of Pittsburgh guided students through mindfulness and yoga rotations. In a separate hands-on session, instructors from the American Heart Association provided students with foundational CPR training to teach basic life-saving skills. During lunch sessions, students attended a panel discussion focused on professional careers in sports. Jim Britt, executive director of SportsPITTSBURGH, served as moderator. The panel featured Rachel Brecht, chief people officer of the Pittsburgh Penguins; Ethan Lounsbury, senior director of marketing for the Pittsburgh Riverhounds; and Benjamin Moore, senior sports marketing manager at F.N.B. item.title: Pep Guardiola says how Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry worked

Regarded as two of the greatest soccer players of the modern generation, Argentina’s Lionel Messi and Portugal’s Cristiano Ronaldo shared one of the most intense soccer rivalries. While Messi represented FC Barcelona, Ronaldo was a main player of their rival team, Real Madrid. Former FC Barcelona manager Pep Guardiola believes that Ronaldo and Messi would not have enjoyed such long and dominant careers without each other. Messi and Ronaldo faced each other multiple times while representing Real Madrid and Barcelona, respectively, and even captained their national team at this year’s FIFA World Cup despite being in the twilight of their careers. However, both men have now retired from international soccer. Recently, speaking on RomárioTV, Guardiola shared his thoughts on their rivalry . “I think the two of them helped each other a great deal, if Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter. But they had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him.'” (via ESPN) Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ronaldo, 41, retired from Portugal as the leading men’s international goal scorer with 146 goals in 234 games. He was recently also awarded the Ballon d’Or of All-Time . Ronaldo also recently scored his 987th career goal. On the other hand, Messi currently captains Inter Miami in MLS and retired with 126 goals for Argentina in 206 games . Ronaldo and Messi’s rivalry dominated soccer for over a decade, and the duo has a total of 13 combined Ballon d’Ors. item.title: Germany's Freigang to miss women's World Cup due do doping ban
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Germany's Laura Freigang pictured during a training Session Open to the Media Ahead of World Cup Qualifier. (is associated with: «Germany's Freigang to miss women's World Cup due do doping ban») Marc Schüler/dpa Germany national team player Laura Freigang will miss next year's women's World Cup in Brazil after she's been suspended for missing doping tests, the German Football Federation (DFB) said in a statement on Thursday. Freigang will be suspended until October 7, 2027 after she reached a settlement with the DFB, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and Germany's National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA). Proceedings against Freigang had been ongoing for months. The 28-year-old was accused of not being at the location she specified for a doping control on three occasions between March 2025 and February 2026. In June, the Eintracht Frankfurt captain explained that the missed tests "were not deliberately avoided appointments but inconsistencies or misunderstandings in the comprehensive details that have to be updated daily and which we as national team players have to update in the system on a daily and hourly basis." Freigang has 45 caps for Germany and has scored 17 goals, but hasn't been a regular starter recently.

item.title: Cole Hutson Could Join His Brother in One of the NHL’s Most Exclusive Clubs
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Only four defensemen have led all NHL rookies in scoring over the course of a season since 1943-44. One of them was Lane Hutson, who recorded 66 points with the Montreal Canadiens in 2024-25. Just two seasons later, his younger brother has a legitimate opportunity to become the fifth. Cole Hutson took over the NHL rookie scoring lead after recording three assists in the Washington Capitals’ 7-4 loss to the New Jersey Devils on Nov. 14. At the time, Hutson was the only defenseman among the league’s top 13 rookie scorers. The 20-year-old has since been overtaken by some of the young forwards having incredible rookie seasons of their own, but he scored his sixth goal of the season in Wednesday’s 7-3 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers, bringing him up to 16 points in 22 games and within four points of rookie scoring leader Roman Kantserov. Considering some of the talent that entered the league this season, the fact that we’re even having this conversation about Hutson is pretty remarkable. Cole Hutson Could Join Some Incredible Company Bobby Orr became the first defenseman in the NHL’s modern era to lead all rookies in scoring, recording 41 points with the Boston Bruins in 1966-67. It took another 22 years for a defenseman to accomplish the feat, with Brian Leetch recording 71 points for the New York Rangers in 1988-89. Quinn Hughes became the third with 53 points for the Vancouver Canucks in 2019-20 before Lane joined the group with his incredible rookie season in Montreal. Cole is currently scoring at a rate that would see him finish with roughly 61 points over an 84-game season. It would be an incredible accomplishment on its own, but imagine both Hutson brothers leading their respective rookie classes in scoring just two years apart. Neither was even selected in the first round of their draft. The Canadiens selected Lane 62nd overall in 2022, while the Capitals selected Cole 43rd overall in 2024. There are going to be plenty of conversations in the coming years about how so many teams managed to pass on both of them. The Capitals Are Giving Hutson an Opportunity To Thrive I wrote earlier this week about how the Capitals may have found a long-term defense partner for Hutson in Jack St. Ivany . At the time, St. Ivany had spent more than 77% of his five-on-five ice time with Washington alongside Hutson, and what I’ve really liked about their partnership is how comfortable St. Ivany has been letting Hutson go to work offensively. Capitals head coach Spencer Carbery has spoken about St. Ivany’s ability to recognize when Hutson is getting involved offensively and adjust his positioning accordingly. When you’ve got a defenseman as talented and creative as Hutson, finding him a partner who understands how to play off him can go a long way toward getting the most out of his abilities. item.title: Jason Kelce has perfect response to bizarre Mike McCarthy ice cream sandwich revelation
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images Jason Kelce has shared a hilarious reaction to reports that Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand. The former Philadelphia Eagles center shared a picture of the frozen treat on social media, seemingly showing his support for McCarthy’s unusual arrangement. The bizarre story emerged amid the messy fallout between McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers, who Pittsburgh officially released on Wednesday. Former Steelers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko, who played for the team in 2023, then revealed that a player told him McCarthy had someone who delivers ice cream sandwiches. “Text from a Pittsburgh Steelers player just now: ‘McCarthy has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand’,” Fehoko posted. His revelation quickly caught the attention of NFL fans, but reporter Jordan Schultz decided to investigate the claims himself. “I asked several Steelers players if Mike McCarthy really does have an ice cream sandwich assistant, and they all confirmed: yes, it’s true,” Schultz revealed. The reporter’s findings suggested the rumour was not simply a joke circulating online. Kelce was among those who could not resist reacting to the revelation. The former Eagles star posted a picture of an ice cream sandwich on X alongside a short but brilliant caption. “I just want to say… I get it,” Kelce wrote. While Rodgers’ departure and his public disagreement with McCarthy have dominated NFL headlines, the Steelers head coach’s alleged ice cream arrangement has provided an unexpected distraction. Although it is hardly a major issue in isolation, it adds to growing concerns about McCarthy’s professionalism . item.title: Wild NHL fight goes on forever — and teammates’ reaction says it all
item.description: Tyrel Bauer #77 of the Winnipeg Jets and Tanner Jeannot #84 of the Boston Bruins fight during a game at TD Garden in Boston, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. BOSTON — Boston’s Tanner Jeannot and Winnipeg’s Tyrel Bauer squared off at center ice in the first period on Wednesday night and put on one of the longest fights seen in the NHL in a while. The 6-foot-3 Bauer and the 6-2 Jeannot dropped the gloves near the center circle, then circled for about 20 seconds, looking for the right moment to make their move, before throwing more than 40 punches over nearly a minute in the Jets’ 4-2 victory over the Bruins. Not every punch landed, but Bauer’s helmet was knocked off, Jeannot got spun around, and when it was over and they were in the penalty box, both benches emptied, and the players went over to fist pound their respective teammates. Tyrel Bauer #77 of the Winnipeg Jets and Tanner Jeannot #84 of the Boston Bruins fight during a game at TD Garden in Boston, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. NHLI via Getty Images “One of the best fights I’ve seen,” said Bruins second-year coach Marco Sturm, who played in the NHL for 14 seasons. “Jeano, holy moly,” Sturm said. “Unbelievable.” Jeannot and Bauer were seen on the ice talking during warmups and, likely, planned to square off. Talk about letting the boys go What a fight pic.twitter.com/ZPDZTDuD5G — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) November 26, 2026 They earned the respect of their teammates by trying to boost the energy for their respective teams. “That’s just two really tough customers,” said Jets center Morgan Barron, who scored a second-period go-ahead goal. “You see Tyrel in those fights, he stands in there as long as the other guy is willing to. I think it was just great, it got the guys some energy. That’s a really difficult job to do.” The Bruins felt the same way. “It’s unbelievable,’’ said Boston center Fraser Minten of Jeannot. “He’s like the nicest guy, an unbelievable teammate. Just an absolute warrior out there.” The Boston Bruins bench looks on as a first-period fight between Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, at TD Garden in Boston. NHLI via Getty Images Sturm has certainly seen his share of “tough guys” or what the league used to call “enforcers,” but he has great respect for what the two had to do. “I came in as young kid in this league and all the fights were pretty much open and you just go,” he said. “There was no defense, no structure. You just: ‘Go, Go.’ “That was wild,” he said. “In today’s world, there’s a lot of technique. … In today’s game, I think Jeano is elite and he showed it today.”

item.title: Where RBL currently stand in the race for the UCL play-offs
item.description: Where RBL currently stand in the race for the UCL play-offs Following our 3-1 win over RC Lens , the Red Bulls now sit 23rd in the table , putting us in a play-off spot. There are three games left in the Champions League league phase, and we're determined to pick up as many points as possible ! “ Every game is important now , which is why today's win was so valuable. We've still got a few games to play and we want to try and pick up as many points as possible. Every point counts ,” Antonio Nusa said afterwards. Manchester United clash could prove pivotal for RBL Automatic qualification for the Champions League round of 16 still looks some way off, with four points separating us from eighth-placed Manchester City . Having already faced two of the competition's strongest sides in Real Madrid and Manchester City during the first half of the league phase, we've got three challenging but winnable games ahead of us . A win away at Manchester United in two weeks' time would see us leapfrog the Red Devils, who currently sit 19th with seven points. United drew 2-2 with Sporting CP on matchday 5 under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino . It's been a difficult season for the English side, who currently sit second from bottom in the Premier League . Our two remaining opponents, Shakhtar Donetsk (26th) and Feyenoord (32nd), are both below us in the standings. They suffered 1-0 defeats to Fenerbahçe and Porto respectively. “We'll go to Manchester full of belief” RBL are off to the iconic Old Trafford on 8th December, where we've got some unfinished business. We suffered a 5-0 defeat in Manchester back in 2020, but won the reverse fixture 3-2 at the Red Bull Arena . “We've been making good progress as a team for several weeks now. We'll go to Manchester full of belief and try to get all three points. It won't be easy, but we'll be ready and we'll fight ,” said Martín Demichelis . Nine points were enough to secure a play-off spot last season, while 11 were needed in 2024/25 , the first season under the new league phase format. We missed out on the knockout stages that year, finishing with just three points. With three games and nine points up for grabs, the Red Bulls have one clear goal : reaching the Champions League round of 16 for the first time since 2023/24. item.title: Real Madrid superstar equals Ferenc Puskas’ record with goal against PSV
item.description: Real Madrid superstar equals Ferenc Puskas’ record with goal against PSV Real Madrid staged an excellent second-half comeback to secure a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League this midweek. Kylian Mbappe scored a brace and was subsequently nominated for the UCL Player of the Week . But the Frenchman had actually gifted his MOTM award to Vinicius Jr. It was an important game for the Brazilian international, who scored for Real Madrid for the first time in three months. In doing so, he has achieved a key milestone. Vinicius Jr. levels Puskas’ record Thanks to his late goal against PSV, Vinicius has now netted his 35th goal for Real Madrid in the Champions League, drawing him level with club legend Ferenc Puskas, reports Defensa Central . It was a special night for Vinicius. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Vinicius Jr. now stands fifth in the all-time list of goalscorers for Real Madrid in the competition, behind only an iconic quartet of Alfredo Di Stefano (49), Raul Gonzalez (66), Karim Benzema (78) and Cristiano Ronaldo (105). This is quite the achievement for a player who has been central to Real Madrid’s recent success and has already bagged two Champions League trophies. In the overall scheme of things, Vinicius currently sits 24th, just one goal behind Puskas. His teammate Kylian Mbappe is further ahead in fifth spot with 76 goals, but a majority of them came in PSG colours. A touching show of unity Apart from the milestone, it was a special goal for Vinicius in many ways, as the forward has been struggling with form throughout the entirety of the season so far. Vinicius Jr. has shown early signs of promise. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) That is why the Real Madrid team showed exceptional unity when the Brazilian international did eventually find the back of the net, with Mbappe being at the heart of it. Despite being named the MOTM, the Frenchman handed the award to Vinicius, in a gesture of recognition for his efforts on the night. Vinicius Jr. himself was moved by the gesture and thanked his teammates after the game. “Very happy for how my teammates have celebrated a goal that I needed. We are a family. Thank you very much, really. I love you all, let’s go for more!” he wrote after the game. This chimes in well with reports that the entire Real Madrid team are now all in on helping Vini get back to his best.

item.title: Al-Nassr slam the door on Joao Felix's Barcelona return as Portuguese star agrees €12m salary hike and 2029 extension
item.description: Al Nassr v Neftchi Fargona - AFC Champions League Elite - Getty Images Sport Joao Felix appears set to remain in Saudi Arabia for the long term after Al-Nassr moved to activate a significant extension in his contract. Despite persistent links suggesting a potential return to Barcelona, the Portuguese international has reportedly given the green light to stay in Riyadh until 2029. Commitment to the Saudi project Al-Nassr have moved decisively to secure the long-term future of Felix, informing the forward of their decision to extend his stay in the Saudi Pro League through to 2029. During a recent high-level meeting between the club's sporting management and the player, the Riyadh-based outfit made it clear that they have no intention of selling the star or rescinding the extension clause in his current agreement. This development follows a period of heavy speculation regarding the 27-year-old’s next career move. According to Arriyadiyah , The former Atletico Madrid man has reportedly welcomed the proposal with open arms, expressing his immense satisfaction with life in Saudi Arabia. Felix highlighted the positive environment at Al-Nassr as a primary reason for his resurgence, which recently earned him a recall to the Portuguese national team starting line-up. His comfort in the city of Riyadh and his strong relationship with the club hierarchy played a pivotal role in the swift negotiations that have now paved the way for his continued presence in the Middle East. Greg, Minnie, and Fred revisit Nebraska’s thrilling 31–28 victory over Ohio State, discussing the Huskers’ resilience, improved offensive line play, and renewed commitment to running the football under Glenn Thomas. item.title: James Jones says Aaron Rodgers’ rant on Pat McAfee’s show wasn’t even the most disappointing part
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ rant on the Pat McAfee show has shaken the NFL, but his former teammate James Jones is more disappointed by what happened on the show itself. The sanctity of the locker room was broken in astonishing fashion by Aaron Rodgers recently on the Pat McAfee show. Following his benching against the Denver Broncos, Rodgers went off on the Pittsburgh Steelers and head coach Mike McCarthy. What happened on the Pat McAfee show was hard to digest, but Rodgers’ former teammate, James Jones, is more disappointed by what happened around it. James Jones calls out AJ Hawk on Pat McAfee show Coincidentally, when Rodgers was going off on the Steelers and McCarthy, AJ Hawk was among the panellists on the Pat McAfee show. Hawk is a Super Bowl winner with the Green Bay Packers, played under McCarthy for nine years, and was also Rodgers’ teammate during that same span. Considering the statements Rodgers was saying with abandon on the show, James Jones felt disappointed that Hawk didn’t interrupt him once. Jones was a part of that same locker room, and hit back at Rodgers’ claim while speaking on Speakeasy . He said: “Coach Mike and Aaron have been with each other for almost 15 years, more than half of his career. And the most disappointing thing in this too on the Pat McAfee show is that AJ Hawk is sitting there. I don’t remember any of this at the Packers. “If you are from where I’m from, if I have a problem with you, I will call you and tell you that. I’m not going to go to the Pat McAfee show and downplay or talk badly about you.” Rodgers perhaps wouldn’t have expected the majority of the NFL ecosystem to side with McCarthy instead of him, but that is what the gravity of the situation is. The way he threw everyone under the bus at the Steelers after being benched was not very leader-like, and is especially not expected of a veteran of the game. Rodgers has probably ended his chances of landing with another NFL team after this. If that’s the case, it’s a sad end to one of the more illustrious careers in the league. item.title: MAC admits error on overturned Kent State touchdown that decided Eastern Michigan’s season finale
item.description: The Mid-American Conference said Wednesday that its replay official got the final play of the Kent State Golden Flashes’ season wrong, and that the touchdown wiped off the board in Tuesday night’s 17-12 loss to the Eastern Michigan Eagles should have counted. Kent State faced fourth-and-9 from the Eastern Michigan 14-yard line with six seconds left when Ethan Thanthanavong found Wayne Harris in the end zone. The officials on the field ruled it a touchdown, which would have put the Golden Flashes ahead in Ypsilanti. The replay review overturned it, ruling that Harris did not have firm control of the ball until his left foot was off the ground and that his right foot then landed out of bounds. The pass went down as incomplete, and Eastern Michigan held on. Samson Evans rushes for a big gain. Associated Press In its postgame evaluation, the league found that the video showed only slight movement of the football and did not establish that Harris lacked or lost control of it. “The video evidence did not meet the clear and obvious standard required to overturn the ruling on the field. The decision to overturn the touchdown was incorrect, and the original ruling should have been upheld,” the MAC said . The conference added that it regretted the effect the error had on the outcome. Kent State’s record still stands at 3-9 and 2-6 in MAC play, and the season is over, so the statement is all the Golden Flashes get for a catch the league now says was a game-winner. News: The MAC says Kent State’s game-winning touchdown at EMU last night should NOT have been overturned. https://t.co/F2GL5AjjrQ https://t.co/8S4AmmWbgF — Chris Vannini (@ChrisVannini) November 25, 2026 Eastern Michigan ended the Chris Creighton era the same day The statement landed hours after Eastern Michigan announced that it and Chris Creighton had parted ways after 13 seasons. The last win of his tenure is one his own conference has now said should have gone the other way. Creighton went 66-90 with the Eagles, and those 66 wins rank second in school history. He took Eastern Michigan to six bowl games, including three straight from 2021 to 2023, and his 2022 team went 9-4 and won the Famous Idaho Potato Bowl for the program’s first bowl victory since 1987. Every season since then has ended with a losing record. The disputed result did not move Eastern Michigan’s postseason status in either direction. At 5-7, the Eagles finished a win short of bowl eligibility, and a 4-8 finish would have left them in the same place. A touchdown on the final snap would have sent Kent State into the offseason with a conference road win. Harris’ catch instead stays in the books as an incomplete pass, and the final score in Ypsilanti remains 17-12, now with the league’s written acknowledgment that the first call on the field was right. item.title: Barcelona optimistic about veteran duo returning from injury against Deportivo – report
item.description: Barcelona optimistic about veteran duo returning from injury against Deportivo – report Barcelona are optimistic that Rodri and Andreas Christensen will be available for Sunday’s La Liga visit to Deportivo de A Coruna, with both players scheduled to undergo a final fitness test in Friday’s training session. According to Mundo Deportivo , the pair have made encouraging progress from their respective injuries, giving Hansi Flick the possibility of adding two more options to his squad for the match, which will be played on November 29. Mind you, neither return is confirmed, however, and Friday’s assessment will determine whether they are ready to be included. Rodri’s recovery offers Barcelona midfield boost Rodri is recovering from a minor injury to the biceps femoris in his right leg, sustained during Barcelona’s Champions League match against Aston Villa on November 3. The midfielder has been feeling positive about his recovery, and the aforementioned outlet believes he is likely to be available against Deportivo. Barcelona are optimistic that Rodri will play against Deportivo. (Picture credit: Barcelona official website) His return would be timely for Flick, as Rodri has missed important matches against Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and Sabah. The club will nevertheless need to assess his readiness and is expected not to rush him back. Even with a demanding run of fixtures approaching, a short appearance could help him regain match fitness ahead of more important games. Christensen also close to returning Meanwhile, Christensen has been s idelined by discomfort in his left calf , which ruled him out of Barcelona’s recent matches against Villarreal and Sabah. The Danish defender has also progressed well and will face the same final test as Rodri. Andreas Christensen did not play against Villarreal and Sabah. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) His potential return would provide Flick with another option in central defence, an area where Barcelona have recently dealt with several fitness problems. Christensen’s availability could help reduce the need to rely on players covering unfamiliar positions during a congested schedule, such as Frenkie de Jong, who has played as centre-back against Villarreal and Sabah. Balde and Yamal remain part of the fitness picture Apart from Rodri and Christensen, Barcelona also need to monitor Alejandro Balde, who left the Sabah match with ankle discomfort after an impressive performance. His condition will be assessed following the injury in Baku. Lamine Yamal, meanwhile, did not travel to Azerbaijan because of a minor ankle issue but is expected to be available against Deportivo. As such, the squad did not train today as players recovered from the long journey back from Baku, meaning that Friday’s session will be important not only for Rodri and Christensen, but also for understanding the overall condition of the team.

item.title: Resurfaced clip of Mike McCarthy admitting to lying to secure Dallas Cowboys job goes viral

Many fans questioned how this wasn’t a more talked-about incident, given that McCarthy said that about the Dallas Cowboys, one of the NFL teams that draws a significant amount of media interest. However, others have pointed out that McCarthy was clearly joking. But even if he was, making such a joke during the most important press conference of your career is certainly a poor look. item.title: Liverpool v Man Utd referee made ‘obvious error’ sending off Leny Yoro as written reasons published
item.description: Referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” by giving Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card against Liverpool, an independent regulatory commission unanimously concluded. Yoro was given his marching orders when he hauled down Swedish striker Alexander Isak in the opening stages of last Sunday’s fiery match at Anfield. Debate raged over Isak’s touch and whether goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have collected the ball had Yoro not made contact. Even referees’ chief Howard Webb concluded that the call was “certainly not clearly wrong”, but then Manchester United appealed to the Football Association for wrongful dismissal and successfully removed his one-match ban on Tuesday. Referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” in sending off Manchester United’s Leny Yoro at Liverpool, an independent commission unanimously concluded (Martin Rickett/PA) (PA Wire) The three-person panel’s written reasons were published on Thursday and stated: “The commission members were unanimous that, taking the foul committed by LY (Yoro) out of the scenario, AI (Isak) would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity. “Despite the fact that AI had reached the ball initially, his touch was heavy to the extent that he had in fact lost control of the ball – that control had, in effect, passed to the advancing MUFC goalkeeper who in the view of the commission would have been able to gather or smother the ball before AI could get to it and shoot at goal. “To the mind of the commission, the referee had made an ‘obvious error’ in deciding that AI (Isak) would have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity.” Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, told the Match Officials: Mic’d Up programme which aired on Tuesday, shortly after confirmation the ban had been removed: “There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he (Isak) would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. “The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t. “I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.” (Getty) The FA’s independent panel, which was made up of former Blackburn and Middlesbrough winger Stuart Ripley, former Sheffield United and Notts County forward Tony Agana and ex-Walsall goalkeeper Mick Kearns, disagreed. The reasons confirm that United submitted technical information to the panel which concluded Isak would have been, at best, 1.8 metres short of the ball even if Yoro had not made the challenge. The reasons state that the commission “had no way of testing the validity of this analysis undertaken by the club and as such the evidence was viewed with caution and allocated weight accordingly”. item.title: Liberty enters final week with NCAA probation after tampering case involving three staffers
item.description: The NCAA’s Division I Committee on Infractions released its decision in the Liberty Flames’ tampering case on Tuesday, putting the No. 21 program on probation as it heads into the final week of a 10-1 regular season. Assistant coaches Newland Isaac and Tony Washington and director of player personnel Colton Korn had impermissible contact with two players, and with representatives for those players, while the athletes were enrolled at another NCAA school and had not entered the transfer portal. The Associated Press identified that school as the Monmouth Hawks. Neither player ended up transferring to Liberty. Liberty, the three staffers and the NCAA enforcement staff agreed on the violations and penalties through the negotiated resolution process, and a hearing panel signed off on the deal. The school receives one year of probation and a $25,000 fine , along with three-week bans on football recruiting communication and unofficial visits during the 2026-27 academic year. Isaac and Korn each received a one-year show-cause order and a one-game suspension, served Sept. 5 against the James Madison Dukes. Head coach Jamey Chadwell was held responsible under the NCAA’s head coach responsibility rules, though the parties agreed he did not know about the contact, in part because of significant health issues, and did not condone it. item.description: Landon Hall was in Ann Arbor last weekend for the Michigan Wolverines’ 18-16 triple-overtime win over the then-No. 4 UCLA Bruins, the only loss on UCLA’s 10-1 record. He left with a scholarship offer from the coaching staff after the game and committed to Michigan on Wednesday. The Class of 2027 quarterback from Penn High School in Indiana told Hayes Fawcett of Rivals that he picked the Wolverines over the Miami (OH) RedHawks and the Eastern Michigan Eagles. Fawcett lists him at 6-foot-3 and 210 pounds. item.title: USC president makes decision on Trojan Marching Band after members vandalize UCLA football facility
item.description: Letters went missing overnight Tuesday from the sign outside the UCLA Bruins’ Wasserman Football Center, and by Wednesday night the president of the University of Southern California had traced the damage to members of his own school’s marching band. What remained on the side of the building spelled out a lewd phrase, and photos of it were circulating online before the morning was over. A UCLA student reported the vandalism to campus police, the Daily Bruin’s Amanda Velasco reported . USC President Beong-Soo Kim then announced in a letter that the Trojan Marching Band will not perform before the game or at halftime when the USC Trojans visit UCLA at the Rose Bowl on Saturday. Administrators and band leadership made the decision together, and Kim presented it as a show of respect toward UCLA and time for the band to reflect. Jan 2, 2023; Arlington, Texas, USA; A view of the USC Trojans helmets and Cotton Bowl logo during the game between the USC Trojans and the Tulane Green Wave in the 2023 Cotton Bowl at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports “This conduct runs contrary to USC’s values and is unacceptable. We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway. “We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community. Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA’s campus last night has no place in this tradition,” Kim wrote . USC’s Tommy Trojan statue and UCLA’s Bruin Bear are usually wrapped and guarded before the game, and USC students have spray-painted UCLA statues, including the Bruin Bear and the John Wooden statue, in past years. This case involves members of a university-sanctioned group, and the consequence falls on every member of the band, including those who had no part in it. UCLA’s entire statement to the Daily Bruin was “Go Bruins” and “Beat SC!” A Rose Bowl meeting with Big Ten title stakes UCLA enters Saturday at 10-1 and No. 9 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and a win keeps its path to the Big Ten Championship Game in its own hands. USC sits at No. 15 with three losses and can still get to the Dec. 5 title game in Indianapolis, but the Trojans need a win and help from elsewhere in the conference. Jul 29, 2022; Los Angeles, CA, USA; A detailed view of UCLA Bruins helmet during Pac-12 Media Day at Novo Theater. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports It is also the first meeting between the two programs as ranked teams since 2022, when No. 7 USC beat No. 16 UCLA 48-45 at the Rose Bowl. This year’s game will be played without the band that normally takes the field before kickoff and at halftime. Kim said any student found responsible will face discipline under university policy, and that interim actions are already being taken while the investigation continues. item.description: The Baylor Bears went looking for a head coach with deep Texas roots after firing Dave Aranda on Oct. 25, and their search is now focused on Jeff Traylor of the UTSA Roadrunners. USA TODAY Sports’ John Brice reported Wednesday that Baylor is expected to move forward with Traylor before the end of the week, barring something unforeseen. Brice cited nine people with knowledge of the search, a group that includes college coaches, NFL assistants and agents. No deal has been finalized. item.description: World football’s governing body, Fifa , has been targeted in a cyberattack that compromised what it describes as a "limited set of personal and business information," it confirmed on Thursday. The three candidates up for election as FIFA president, Gianni Infantino, Kohzo Tashima and Philippe Diallo (AP) "FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," the governing body said in its statement. The University of Southern California has barred its own marching band from playing Saturday at the iconic Rose Bowl, where the school’s football team is set to take on rival UCLA in a major college football matchup. Kim issued a letter explaining the decision, writing: “This conduct runs contrary to USC’s values and is unacceptable. We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway.” ESPN reported: One of those actions is the decision not to have the band’s on-field performances at the Rose Bowl on Saturday “out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university’s values,” per Kim. “We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community,” Kim said. “Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA’s campus last night has no place in this tradition.” The game is a big one, as it’s the first time the two schools have played against each other in football as ranked teams since 2022. item.title: Gazzaniga: "The most important thing was to build a team and be all together."
item.description: Gazzaniga: "The most important thing was to build a team and be all together." Paulo Gazzaniga has highlighted the unity within Girona's locker room. The red-and-white goalkeeper values the team's current moment beyond the results: "Not just because of the results, but also because of what you can see: the unity, the team, and the effort we put into every match." Gazzaniga believes there is still room for improvement in their play, but he feels that the work to build team spirit is already evident on the pitch: "But the most important thing was to build a team and be united, and I think that has been visible for several matches now." The goalkeeper also explained how he uses his position to help his teammates. From behind the central defenders, he can follow movements like the forwards' runs, which are not always as visible from other areas of the field: "I’m lucky to see the whole field, and maybe that gives me a bit more of an advantage when it comes to communicating with my teammates." Gazzaniga also reflected on his four years at Girona: "I’m very happy and grateful to have been here these four years." The goalkeeper recalls that last season was the most difficult, but he doesn’t think it overshadows the good moments he has experienced at the club. He arrived in Girona at the age of 30 and values having been able to play matches, gain minutes, and acquire experience. From his daily routine, he cherishes the simplest things: "I think the routine is what I like the most: coming to train, seeing my teammates, and enjoying what we do." The Argentine also took a moment to talk about his family. He mentioned that when he arrived in Girona, his eldest son was one year old. Now he is five and has a younger brother who is one year old. Gazzaniga recalled the role of his father, who was also a goalkeeper, and explained that just as he grew up watching his father play, now it is his children who watch him. As for whether they will follow in his footsteps, he is clear: "I just want them to be happy and do what they love." Finally, the goalkeeper recalled that he was close to facing his brother Gianfranco when he had just joined Rayo and his brother was a goalkeeper at Almeria. Paulo played that match, but his brother wasn’t there. "I would have liked to have my brother in front of me, but well, it’s difficult." Now, if another opportunity arises, he knows the decision isn’t his: "In the end, it doesn’t depend on us; it depends on the coaches, on the team." This situation could happen next Tuesday at El Alcoraz. His brother is the goalkeeper for Huesca, the team the red-and-whites will face in the Copa del Rey knockout round.

item.title: Richard Jefferson says there’s a change the NBA needs to make around Thanksgiving
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images Thanksgiving is upon us but NBA fans will be left wanting as there are no games scheduled to take place on November 26, something Richard Jefferson is keen to see change. By comparison, NFL supporters have three blockbuster games to look forward to on Thursday, including a particularly big meeting between the 9-1 Buffalo Bills and the 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs. Now, Richard Jefferson has called for the NBA to bring back games on Thanksgiving, saying he ‘mainly’ wants it to happen because football started putting matchups on TV during Christmas Day. Richard Jefferson wants NBA to bring back Thanksgiving games Speaking on the Road Trippin’ Show, he said: “The answer is 100% yes. They should bring back Thanksgiving games. “First of all, the fact that the NFL – listen, I know none of us is going to be working, so yes, it would impact us, but let’s just play the hype. Yes, they should. Why? Because the NFL disrespected us and started trying to have games on Christmas Day. They’re trying to take our audience. They’re trying to mess with us. Christmas Day belongs to us, but if y’all want to play that game, then let’s just start playing hoop games, right? “So now, all of a sudden, when you’re watching whoever versus whoever and the score is 42-7, you can switch the channel and turn on a basketball game. So do I believe in it? Yes, I do, mainly because they want to start messing with Christmas Day.” The NBA, then known as the Basketball Association of America, started showing games on Thanksgiving back in 1946. That tradition lasted until 1982 before eventually returning from 1994 to 2006. There were then no games in 2007 before the NBA scheduled fixtures on the holiday again from 2008 to 2010. However, the NBA lockout in 2011 once again brought a halt to the action on Thanksgiving and there have been no matches since. At present, the ‘Holidays’ section of the league’s Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) does not actually make any reference to the November holiday, instead only referencing Christmas, New Year’s and Good Friday. In turn, even if some inside the NBA may wish for it to return, they may find it difficult to get players to agree to a change in schedule. item.title: NFL Gross Quarterback Rankings: A not-so-fond farewell for Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Six teams were on their bye in Week 11. That meant six quarterbacks got the chance to figure their stuff out. For a backup thrust into the spotlight like Tommy DeVito, that means trying to reclaim the glory of his most meme-able plays. For Michael Penix Jr., it means grinding tape and tweaking a playbook that's seen him tantalize Atlanta Falcons fans before balancing big plays with gruesome mistakes. And for everyone else, it meant ignoring those guys and trying to figure out what the hell is going on in Pittsburgh . Aaron Rodgers makes what could be his final appearance in these rankings after (gestures broadly) . But who else was gross enough to join him in Week 11? There's no perfect metric for a quarterback's impact, but expected points added (EPA) helps measure their ability to swing the outcome of a game through the air, on the ground and through avoiding negative plays. Last year, EPA told us Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford were a cut above the rest of the league's quarterbacks in the regular season, netting 151.3 and 120.3 EPA , respectfully. No one else in the league topped triple digits. Unsurprisingly, those two led playoff teams and finished second and first, respectively, in MVP voting. We can use EPA to help dissect which quarterbacks underwhelmed the hardest in their debut. By comparing their Week 11 EPA across their early 2026 season averages, we get a better idea of whose fans should be most annoyed. And so, we end up with a "worst QBs" list that doesn't include some of the league's actual worst quarterbacks, simply because their starts to the season have been so disappointing we've been moderately conditioned not to expect more this fall. You have to be at least decent in 2026 — or otherworldly awful on a given week — to wind up in the gross QB rankings. We'll also look at completion percentage over expected (CPOE), which gives you a good idea of which quarterbacks are making tough throws (and, in some cases, being bailed out by exceptional catches). All data come from NFL Pro. We'll also keep a running tally of the times each quarterback lands here. We'll score that placement track meet style — 10 points for first place, then eight, six, four, two and one — in order to figure out who was truly 2026's grossest passer. While it was slightly alarming to see the New Orleans Saints' 24th-ranked defense bottle him up, he still got a win that keeps Chicago's momentum rolling into a Thanksgiving showdown with the Detroit Lions. item.title: Barnsley players 'letting the badge down' - McGeehan
item.description: Cameron McGeehan has scored nine goals in 17 appearances in all competitions this season [Shutterstock] Barnsley captain Cameron McGeehan says the players are "consumed" by the team's poor form. The Reds are winless in the league since 2 September and are four points adrift of the safety line at the bottom of League One. Their run of 11 league games without a win is their second longest below the top two divisions in their history. "It's our lives, we take it home with us and you don't really switch off, especially at times like this, it consumes you," the midfielder told BBC Radio Sheffield. "We're letting the badge down at the minute and you wear that every day and try and put it right." The South Yorkshire side have taken just one point from their past eight matches. Some travelling fans chanted that the players were "not fit to wear the shirt" after Tuesday's 3-0 defeat at Bradford City. McGeehan, 31, said the team were trying to "draw a line in the sand" from that match when they travel to Wimbledon on Saturday. "It's never nice but we are putting it right and we've got a massive game on Saturday and we're trying to draw a line in the sand and say no more," he added. "We just need to bring it back to winning a game and try and get the fans back on side because we need them more than ever. "They've been great, they've stuck with us and we know we haven't been good enough and results haven't been good. We can completely understand their frustration." 'Boring' talking about good performances Despite the 3-0 scoreline, Barnsley had 23 shots to Bradford's 10 on Tuesday and their previous five defeats to that had all come in 2-1 losses. McGeehan, who returned to the club for a second spell in the summer, said the team were not turning performances into points. "Everyone keeps saying 'that was a good performance' and it's boring talking about that, we need to find a way of being better at getting results," he said. "You saw the other night we had all the ball and we're not making the most of it in terms of scoring and conceding. "It's more frustrating because you think there's a good team in there and a lot of potential but putting that into points is the biggest thing and we're trying to figure that out and get it going as quickly as possible." item.title: LeBron James reveals why he doesn’t ‘dominate every night’ for the Philadelphia 76ers
item.description: Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images LeBron James knows his role with the Philadelphia 76ers, but against the Miami Heat, he definitely got the green light, which led to his first triple-double with the franchise. The 41-year-old scored 25 points, grabbed 10 rebounds and made 12 assists in the 76ers’ 111-104 win against the Heat, who had won seven games in a row leading up to the game. He looked in great rhythm, as he shot 60% from the field and went 4-for-6 from three-point range. In a game where Joel Embiid was absent and Jaylen Brown went down due to an injury in the third quarter, LBJ knew that he had to take over the game if the 76ers needed the win. However, the four-time NBA champion made an interesting point to explain why these kind of performances would be rare for him with the 76ers. LeBron James outlines why he is not dominating every game for the Philadelphia 76ers When James chose Philly as his destination, fans in the city were extremely happy, as the franchise had added an all-time great player to an already strong roster. There were reservations about how things were going to work out with James, Brown, Embiid and Tyrese Maxey all needing the ball. But the 76ers have figured it out, and it has needed James to take a role behind the other stars. “I don’t think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club. We have a Finals MVP, regular season MVP, we got an up and coming superstar point guard, a young fella in V.J., who is up and coming as well. My dues are paid and all done; if they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that, but that’s not my job. But if they need it, I can do it at any given moment,” said James to the media. James led the game in +/- and looked phenomenal from start to finish. After the game, Tyrese Maxey was made aware of James’ comments, and he said: “Dust it off then.” This shows that the players on the 76ers are prepared to allow James to play his game when he wants to. Even when he plays a secondary role, the all-time points record holder is making big plays for the team, which is why he is a piece that will be instrumental to them if they are to end their wait for an NBA championship. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
